Each one\\u0027s handoff follows, in\\ndispatch order \\u2014 the run that opened the work first, its follow-ups after it.\\n\\n[Run 1 of 4 \\u00B7 a18e3b06]\\n\\n- **What now exists.** The store connects unpooled (\\u0060StoreConfiguration.ConnectionStringOf\\u0060). \\u0060HomeStore\\u0060 holds one connection of its own from the first commit until disposal, which keeps \\u0060-wal\\u0060 and \\u0060-shm\\u0060 around. \\u0060tests/Coanda.Tests/Daemon/StoreFiles.ReadOnceClosedAsync\\u0060 reads a home\\u0027s store files only after closing the store. \\u0060ModuleNode.CloseDaemonAsync\\u0060 closes a node\\u0027s daemon but keeps its home. \\u0060SoftwareNode\\u0060 and \\u0060ModuleNode\\u0060 clean up after a failed start, and \\u0060SoftwareNode\\u0060 disposes only once. New tests: \\u0060StoreConnectionTests\\u0060, \\u0060StoreFilesTests\\u0060, \\u0060SoftwareNodeTests\\u0060.\\n- **Gotchas.**\\n  - Never give a store over a home a pooled connection string. Microsoft.Data.Sqlite 10.0.9\\u0027s pool can hand one native connection to two holders, which shows up as Error 5 and as transactions lost to Fisher\\u0027s rollback when a session closes.\\n  - A store that never commits never takes the hold, so its write-ahead log is checkpointed whenever its last session closes.\\n  - \\u0060StoreConnectionTests\\u0060 reach into Microsoft.Data.Sqlite\\u0027s private \\u0060_innerConnection\\u0060, \\u0060_outerConnection\\u0060 and \\u0060_active\\u0060.\\n  - The suite runs about 20% slower.\\n- **Left undone, on purpose.**\\n  - No upstream change. A dotnet/efcore issue about the \\u0060Activate\\u0060 versus \\u0060ReclaimLeakedConnections\\u0060 race could be filed, and Fisher\\u0027s unconditional rollback on session close is worth raising too.\\n  - The flow-run timeout\\u0027s link to the shared connection is reasoned, not proven.\\n  - The RepoFieldTests failure is out of scope, and it didn\\u0027t occur in the 20 runs.\\n  - None of the new tests has run on CI yet.\\n\\n[Run 2 of 4 \\u00B7 74ca2171]\\n\\n- Nothing new exists. A failure that takes about 3 seconds has always meant billing so far.\\n- I deliberately changed no code, because the branch has nothing to fix.
